questions.q: What is the primary purpose of systems software?
o: To store data in tables and records
To let users create documents and presentations
To design graphics and edit images
To run the hardware and support application programs
questions.e: Systems software runs the hardware and provides the platform application programs need.

questions.q: Where does systems software sit in relation to the user and the hardware?
o: As a middle layer between user applications and hardware
Above the user, below the applications
Outside the computer, in the network
questions.e: The lesson describes system software as a middle layer between applications and hardware.

questions.q: Which of the following is a type of systems software?
questions.e: Firmware is one of the five types of systems software.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a systems software type from the lesson?
questions.e: A word processor is application software. The system types are OS, firmware, translators, drivers, and utilities.

questions.q: Firmware is usually stored in which type of memory?
questions.e: Firmware is permanently etched into a hardware device and stored in ROM.

questions.q: Who typically writes firmware for a hardware device?
questions.e: Firmware should only be written once, by the hardware manufacturer.

questions.q: What is the main job of a device driver?
o: To control and manage a particular device at the hardware level
questions.e: A device driver controls a specific device and acts as an interface between the device and the OS.

questions.q: Which pair correctly matches a system utility with its function?
questions.e: Defragmentation reorganizes fragmented files on disk.

questions.q: Programming language translators are best described as what?
o: Mediator programs that translate high-level code to machine-level code
Tools that clean the hard disk
questions.e: Translators mediate between human-readable code and machine-level code.

questions.q: Which statement best defines an operating system?
o: A free app for editing videos
A type of firmware in a printer
The most basic system software, without which other software cannot work
questions.e: The OS is the most basic system software and manages other programs, access, and security.

questions.q: MS-DOS stands for which of the following?
questions.e: MS-DOS means Microsoft Disk Operating System.

questions.q: What type of interface does MS-DOS use?
questions.e: MS-DOS is a non-graphical, command line operating system.

questions.q: MS-DOS was developed for IBM-compatible computers using which microprocessor family?
questions.e: MS-DOS targeted IBM-compatible computers with x86 microprocessors.

questions.q: Which best describes MS-DOS in terms of users?
questions.e: MS-DOS is a single-user operating system: only one user can operate at a time.

questions.q: Why can a mouse NOT be used to operate MS-DOS?
o: It does not support a graphical interface
It only runs on Apple hardware
questions.e: MS-DOS lacks a GUI, so the mouse has nothing to point at.

questions.q: What does it mean that MS-DOS does not support multiprogramming?
o: It can only have one process in RAM
It cannot connect to the internet
questions.e: Without multiprogramming, MS-DOS keeps only one process in RAM at a time.

questions.q: Windows OS is designed to run primarily on which processors?
questions.e: Windows targets standard x86 Intel and AMD processors.

questions.q: What interface did Windows popularize that removed the need to memorize commands?
questions.e: The Windows GUI eliminated the need to memorize command line commands.

questions.q: What does backward compatible mean for Windows?
o: It works only on old computers
Old programs can run on newer versions
questions.e: Backward compatibility lets older programs run on newer Windows versions.

questions.q: Which is a stated advantage of Windows?
o: It automatically detects hardware, removing the need to manually install drivers
It is completely free and open source
It uses the least RAM of any OS
questions.e: Windows automatically detects most hardware and installs drivers.

questions.q: Why is Windows often considered expensive?
o: It only runs on expensive Apple hardware
It requires a paid license and many applications are paid
It requires a monthly internet subscription
questions.e: Windows itself is a paid license and most applications are paid products.

questions.q: What happens to Windows when many programs are loaded at the same time?
o: It slows down and may hang
questions.e: Windows slows and can hang when the user loads many programs at once.

questions.q: Why is Windows especially vulnerable to viruses according to the lesson?
o: It has a huge user base and needs constant security patches
questions.e: Its large user base makes it a bigger target, so users must keep updating security patches.

questions.q: Who developed the Linux operating system?
questions.e: Linux was developed by Linus Torvalds.

questions.q: Linux is based on which earlier operating system?
questions.e: Linux is a freely distributed, cross-platform OS developed based on UNIX.

questions.q: Which best describes Linux licensing?
questions.e: Linux is open source and free to download and use.

questions.q: Portability of Linux means it can do what?
o: Be installed on many types of devices such as mobile and tablets
questions.e: Linux can be installed on various device types, from servers to tablets.

questions.q: Which statement about Linux is correct?
questions.e: Linux is a multi-user, multitasking operating system.

questions.q: What is a common drawback of Linux?
o: It is harder to find applications because it does not dominate the market
It cannot be installed on laptops
It cannot connect to the internet
questions.e: Fewer mainstream applications target Linux compared with Windows.

questions.q: Why might some hardware malfunction under Linux?
questions.e: Driver support can be patchy, causing incompatibility with some hardware.

questions.q: Solaris was originally developed by which company?
questions.e: Solaris, also called SunOS, was Sun's UNIX variant.

questions.q: Solaris was originally developed for which processor architecture?
questions.e: It was built for Scalable Processor Architecture (SPARC) and Intel-based processors.

questions.q: Which company purchased Sun and renamed Solaris?
questions.e: Oracle purchased Sun and renamed the OS Oracle Solaris.

questions.q: Which is a known strength of Solaris?
questions.e: Solaris is known for scalability and handling large workloads.

questions.q: Why was Solaris widely used for websites during the growth of the internet?
o: It became one of the most widely installed server systems for websites
questions.e: As the internet grew, Solaris systems became widely installed web servers.

questions.q: Which statement about Solaris security is correct?
o: It relies only on antivirus apps
questions.e: Solaris has advanced, unique security capabilities.

questions.q: What is a common drawback of Solaris?
o: It is expensive and does not provide free updates
questions.e: Solaris is an enterprise OS and updates are not free.

questions.q: Which weakness of Solaris is mentioned in the lesson?
o: Poor graphical user interface and hardware support
questions.e: Solaris lacks good GUI support and broad hardware support.

questions.q: Symbian OS was based on which architecture?
questions.e: Symbian was the most widely used smartphone OS based on ARM architecture.

questions.q: In what year was Symbian discontinued?
questions.e: Symbian was discontinued in 2014.

questions.q: Symbian was developed through a partnership of which companies?
questions.e: Symbian Ltd was a partnership among PDA and phone makers including Psion, Motorola, Ericsson, and Nokia.

questions.q: Symbian was designed especially for what kind of devices?
o: Smartphones and handheld digital devices with low power needs
questions.e: It targeted low-power, battery-based smartphones and ROM-based devices.

questions.q: Which languages could Symbian run applications written in?
o: Python, Java ME, Flash Lite, Ruby, and .NET
questions.e: Symbian supported apps in Python, Java ME, Flash Lite, Ruby, and .NET.

questions.q: Which is a stated drawback of Symbian?
o: It is not responsive or smooth compared with other OSes
It has too much virtual memory
questions.e: Symbian's responsiveness was not as smooth or sensitive as competing OSes.

questions.q: What memory-related limitation did Symbian have?
questions.e: The lesson lists lack of virtual memory as a Symbian drawback.

questions.q: Android is designed primarily for what type of devices?
o: Touch screen mobile devices such as phones and tablets
questions.e: Android targets touch screen phones and tablets.

questions.q: Which is a key advantage of Android being open source?
o: It is free and anyone can use it
questions.e: Open source means Android is free and usable by anyone.

questions.q: Where do most Android users download apps?
questions.e: The Play Store offers over one million Android apps.

questions.q: What is the Android SDK used for?
questions.e: Developers download the Android Software Development Kit to build apps.

questions.q: Which is a stated drawback of Android?
o: It depends on Java, making intuitive modern interfaces harder to build
questions.e: Its dependency on Java makes designing modern user experiences difficult.

questions.q: Why do Android phones often drain battery quickly?
o: Apps tend to run in the background even after being closed
questions.e: Many apps keep running in the background, draining the battery.

questions.q: When are Android phones most likely to overheat?
o: During heavy graphics or hardcore productivity tasks
questions.e: Overheating is noted during heavy graphics or productivity workloads.

questions.q: iOS was created by which company?
questions.e: iOS is Apple's mobile operating system.

questions.q: Which devices use iOS?
questions.e: iOS is exclusive to Apple's iPhone, iPad, and iPod.

questions.q: Which is a stated strength of iOS?
o: Excellent, intuitive interface and fluid response
It is the most customizable OS
questions.e: iOS is praised for its intuitive UI and fluid response.

questions.q: Why is beta testing on iOS said to take longer?
o: The OS is closed source and limited to selected developers
questions.e: Closed source limits beta testing to a small group of developers.

questions.q: Which is a drawback of iOS apps?
o: They occupy a very large amount of memory space
questions.e: iOS applications take up large amounts of storage.

questions.q: What does the lesson say about third-party installations on iOS?
questions.e: iOS does not allow third-party installations.

questions.q: Why do older devices struggle to run newer iOS versions?
questions.e: iOS is resource intensive, so older hardware struggles with new versions.

questions.q: A company needs an enterprise server OS known for scalability and strong security, regardless of cost. Which is the best fit from the lesson?
questions.e: Solaris is the enterprise, scalability-focused server OS in the lesson.

questions.q: A public school wants a free, open-source OS for old lab computers. Which is the best choice from the lesson?
questions.e: Linux is free, open source, portable, and can revive older hardware.

questions.q: A user's new graphics card is not recognized by the OS. What should be installed?
o: A firmware update for the monitor
questions.e: The OS needs a device driver to communicate with the new card.

questions.q: Which system software would you use to remove temporary files and free disk space?
questions.e: Disk cleaner is a system utility for maintenance.

questions.q: A router's low-level software is permanently stored on a chip and rarely changed. This is an example of what?
questions.e: Embedded, permanently stored device software is firmware.

questions.q: An old Windows program still runs after upgrading to a newer Windows version. Which feature explains this?
questions.e: Backward compatibility allows older programs to run on newer versions.

questions.q: Which pairing of OS and developer is correct?
questions.e: Linux was created by Linus Torvalds.

questions.q: Which OS is described as having the largest user base and the widest software selection?
questions.e: Windows has a very large user base and a large selection of software.

questions.q: Which combination of limitations belongs to MS-DOS?
questions.e: MS-DOS is single-user, command-line only, and cannot multiprogram.

questions.q: Which pairing of a mobile OS and its key drawback is correct?
o: iOS - limited customization and no third-party installs
questions.e: iOS is closed and restricts customization and third-party installs.

questions.q: Which set contains ONLY system utilities?
questions.e: Anti-virus, disk cleaner, and defragmentation are maintenance utilities.

questions.q: A translator that converts high-level source code into machine code is what kind of systems software?
questions.e: Compilers and interpreters are programming language translators.

questions.q: Which is the best example of an operating system managing security and access?
o: Requiring a password before a user can log in
questions.e: Login authentication is an OS access and security function.

questions.q: Which statement about Linux and Windows is accurate?
o: Linux is open source; Windows is proprietary and licensed
questions.e: Linux is open source; Windows is a paid, proprietary OS.

questions.q: A hospital needs mobile devices managed under a closed, security-focused ecosystem with regular patches. Which OS fits best from the lesson?
questions.e: iOS is highlighted for safety, fewer breaches, and regular security updates.

questions.q: Which OS is no longer in active development and was discontinued in 2014?
questions.e: Symbian was discontinued in 2014.

questions.q: Which best explains why MS-DOS is described as lightweight?
questions.e: MS-DOS is lightweight because it uses minimal resources.

questions.q: System software that provides basic functionality required by the user by managing hardware behavior is called what?
questions.e: The OS manages hardware behavior to provide basic functionality.

questions.q: Which sequence correctly orders the flow of a request from user to hardware?
questions.e: System software mediates between applications and hardware.

questions.q: Which of these would be classified as firmware rather than an application?
o: The control program stored in a printer's ROM
questions.e: Firmware is stored in ROM inside a hardware device.

questions.q: Which task belongs to a system utility rather than an application?
questions.e: Defragmentation is system maintenance, not a user productivity task.

questions.q: Name the most basic system software that manages other programs and provides access and security to users.
questions.e: The operating system is the foundational system software.

questions.q: What is the software called that is permanently etched into a hardware device and stored in ROM?
questions.e: Firmware is written once by the manufacturer and stored in ROM.

questions.q: What type of system software translates high-level language code into machine-level code?
questions.e: Programming language translators (compilers and interpreters) perform this conversion.

questions.q: What system software acts as an interface between a particular device and the operating system?
questions.e: Device drivers control specific hardware at the hardware level.

questions.q: What type of system software is used for maintenance and configuration, such as anti-virus and disk cleaner tools?
questions.e: System utilities handle maintenance and configuration tasks.

questions.q: What does the acronym MS-DOS stand for?
questions.e: MS-DOS is Microsoft Disk Operating System.

questions.q: What type of user interface does MS-DOS provide?
questions.e: MS-DOS uses a command line interface, not a GUI.

questions.q: Which open-source operating system was developed by Linus Torvalds?
questions.e: Linux was created by Linus Torvalds and based on UNIX.

questions.q: Which UNIX-based operating system is known for scalability and is now owned by Oracle?
questions.e: Solaris (SunOS) is the scalable UNIX variant now owned by Oracle.

questions.q: Which mobile operating system was discontinued in 2014 and was based on ARM architecture?
questions.e: Symbian was discontinued in 2014.

questions.q: Which open-source mobile operating system was developed primarily for touch screen devices and uses the Play Store?
questions.e: Android is open source and distributes apps through the Play Store.

questions.q: Which mobile operating system is exclusive to iPhone, iPad, and iPod?
questions.e: iOS, short for iPhone OS, is Apple's exclusive mobile OS.

questions.q: What is the term for an OS feature that lets older programs run on newer versions?
questions.e: Backward compatibility preserves support for older programs.

questions.q: What is the graphical interface called that eliminates the need to memorize commands?
questions.e: A GUI uses visual elements instead of typed commands.

questions.q: What is the Android kit called that developers download to build apps?
questions.e: The Android SDK provides tools for app development.

questions.q: Which system utility reduces the size of files on disk?
questions.e: Disk compression software reduces file size to save space.

questions.q: Which system utility rearranges fragmented files to improve performance?
questions.e: Defragmentation reorganizes fragmented data on the disk.

questions.q: Which OS is a paid enterprise UNIX variant that does not provide free updates?
questions.e: Solaris is an expensive enterprise OS without free updates.

questions.q: Which OS is known for having patchier driver support that may cause hardware malfunction?
questions.e: Linux driver support is less uniform, causing some hardware issues.

questions.q: Which OS has the largest user base, a GUI, and is developed by Microsoft for x86 processors?
questions.e: Windows is Microsoft's GUI operating system for x86 hardware.

questions.q: System software acts as a middle layer between user applications and hardware.
questions.e: This is the lesson's core definition of system software.

questions.q: Firmware is [[regularly rewritten by end users]] whenever they install a new application.
questions.e: Firmware is written once by the manufacturer and stored in ROM.

questions.q: MS-DOS supports [[multiple users]] working at the same time.
questions.e: MS-DOS is a single-user operating system.

questions.q: MS-DOS [[supports a graphical user interface]], which is why a mouse is used to operate it.
questions.fix: does not support a graphical user interface
questions.e: MS-DOS is command line only, so a mouse cannot be used.

questions.q: Windows is backward compatible, meaning old programs can run on newer versions.
questions.e: Backward compatibility is listed as a Windows feature.

questions.q: Linux is a [[closed-source]] operating system.
questions.e: Linux is open source and was created by Linus Torvalds.

questions.q: Solaris is known for its [[poor scalability]] and cannot handle large workloads.
questions.e: Solaris is known for scalability and large workloads.

questions.q: Symbian was discontinued in 2014.
questions.e: Symbian was the leading smartphone OS until its 2014 discontinuation.

questions.q: Symbian [[includes a virtual memory system]] for managing memory.
questions.e: Lack of virtual memory is a listed Symbian drawback.

questions.q: Android is an open-source operating system.
questions.e: Android is open source and free for anyone to use.

questions.q: iOS [[allows users to install applications from any third-party source]] without restrictions.
questions.e: A stated iOS drawback is that it does not allow third-party installations.
accept: does not allow third party installations

questions.q: iOS is generally considered safer than other mobile operating systems and has fewer security breaches.
questions.e: iOS is described as safer with fewer breaches and regular patches.

questions.q: Anti-virus software and disk defragmentation are examples of system utilities.
questions.e: These are maintenance and configuration tools.

questions.q: Device drivers act as an interface between a hardware device and the operating system.
questions.e: Drivers let the OS control specific hardware.

questions.q: Windows requires users to [[manually install every device driver]] because it cannot detect hardware automatically.
questions.e: Windows automatically detects hardware and installs drivers.
